issue_context.title: rainbird integration limit of one rainbird controller
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I can not add more than one rainbird ESP-RZXe in home assistant despite documentation is stating that it supports multiple controllers from rainbird.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.8.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

rainbird

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Diagnostics information

I have two rainbird ESP-RZXe with firmware 2.9. I have installed the first it works seamless. When trying to setup a second rainbird controller i receive a timeout at the first time

Logger: homeassistant.components.rainbird.config_flow
Source: components/rainbird/config_flow.py:77
Integration: Rain Bird ([documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/rainbird), [issues](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22integration%3A+rainbird%22))
First occurred: 22:00:38 (3 occurrences)
Last logged: 22:07:04

Error during config flow: Timeout connecting to Rain Bird controller

When retrying to setup it again i get the message that the controller is already set up - but the second rainbird controller doesnt show up. When deleting the first controller and setup the second it works seamless as well. It looks like that there is a limit of maximum one rainbird controller. 

The fallback creating two entries in configuration.yaml doesnt work either. Any ideas? 

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

@1frankrippl can you enable debug logging (described here https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/troubleshooting/#enabling-debug-logging) and provide some additional detail from the logs?

This is not working as intended so trying to understand why this would happen...
Hi, I don't see any failures there. Can you include the context including any failed or error log messages? That all looked successful, but I may be misunderstanding

I see. I think the problem is the devices return the same serial number which is supposed to be a unique id. However both of the devices appear to return "0" for the serial number:
```
2023-09-05 22:38:49.674 DEBUG (MainThread) [pyrainbird.async_client] Response: {'type': 'SerialNumberResponse', 'serialNumber': 0}
```
so they the both can't be registered. I'll think about some options here...

Thank you for the report, so there are additional aspects that need to be updated.

Once fixed, one challenge here may be that these will not be able to have unique IDs which may impact how they can be adjusted in the UI.

review_comments: Looking at this and the attached issue it seems it would be better to remove unique id completely and use `_async_abort_entries_match()` to see if the entry options are matching.

Hi, I may need some additional help to understand. Can you elaborate?

One thing i'd like to clarify is that most devices do have serial numbers, but some devices appear to return a zero. My intent is to keep a unique id for devices that do have a unique id, and not have one for devices that don't have one.

Happy to hear your thoughts in more detail.

Maybe I want both? Use `_async_abort_entries_match` when there is no serial? Sounds like that gives some of the benefits of checking if a unique id already exists (same host:port/password) when there is no unique id?
I was just thinking that since you need to use `_async_abort_entries_match()` for testing when there is no serial why not always use that instead of mixing it together with unique_id.

Serial matching is always best, so using the unique ID would be nice and abort on that if possible. The `_async_abort_entries_match` is nice, but not as robust as working with a unique ID. Therefore, I think the suggestion above by @allenporter makes a lot of sense.
